'''Al-Tayeb Salih''' ({{langx|ar|الطيب صالح|aṭ-Ṭayyib Ṣāliḥ}}; July 12, 1929 – February 18, 2009)<ref name=":nytimes">{{cite web|title=Tayeb Salih, 80, Cross-Cultural Arabic Novelist, Dies|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2009/02/23/books/23salih.html?mtrref=www.google.se&gwh=860B7C877F4F04A13227627A219945CD&gwt=pay&assetType=REGIWALL|publisher=The New York Times|date=February 23, 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210802120519/https://www.nytimes.com/2009/02/23/books/23salih.html?mtrref=www.google.se&gwh=860B7C877F4F04A13227627A219945CD&gwt=pay&assetType=REGIWALL|archive-date=August 2, 2021}}</ref> was a [[Demographics of Sudan|Sudanese]] writer, novelist, and journalist, considered to be one of the most prominent Arab writers of the 20th century. Through his captivating narrative style and profound themes, Salih etched his name alongside literary giants such as [[Gibran Khalil Gibran]], [[Taha Hussein]], and [[Naguib Mahfouz]], earning the title of "the genius of the Arabic novel" by many critics.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Solutions |first=Optimal |title=هذا هو "عبقري الرواية العربية" الذي احتفل به غوغل |trans-title=This is the "genius of the Arabic novel" that Google celebrated |url=https://www.jana.ps/articles/Article/1221/ar/%D9%87%D8%B0%D8%A7_%D9%87%D9%88_%D8%B9%D8%A8%D9%82%D8%B1%D9%8A_%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B1%D9%88%D8%A7%D9%8A%D8%A9_%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B9%D8%B1%D8%A8%D9%8A%D8%A9_%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B0%D9%8A_%D8%A7%D8%AD%D8%AA%D9%81%D9%84_%D8%A8%D9%87_%D8%BA%D9%88%D8%BA%D9%84 |access-date=2025-08-09 |website=مجلة جنى}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2017-07-12 |title=هذا هو "عبقري الرواية العربية" الذي احتفل به غوغل |trans-title=This is the "genius of the Arabic novel" that Google celebrated |url=https://www.alarabiya.net/culture-and-art/2017/07/12/%D9%87%D8%B0%D8%A7-%D9%87%D9%88-%D8%B9%D8%A8%D9%82%D8%B1%D9%8A-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B1%D9%88%D8%A7%D9%8A%D8%A9-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B9%D8%B1%D8%A8%D9%8A%D8%A9-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B0%D9%8A-%D8%A7%D8%AD%D8%AA%D9%81%D9%84-%D8%A8%D9%87-%D8%BA%D9%88%D8%BA%D9%84 |access-date=2025-08-09 |website=العربية |language=ar}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=رابطة أدباء الشام - عبقري الرواية العربية " الطيب صالح " |trans-title=The League of Levant Writers - The Genius of the Arabic Novel "Tayeb Salih" |url=https://www.odabasham.net/%D9%81%D9%86%D9%88%D9%86/22743-%D8%B9%D8%A8%D9%82%D8%B1%D9%8A-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B1%D9%88%D8%A7%D9%8A%D8%A9-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B9%D8%B1%D8%A8%D9%8A%D8%A9--%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B7%D9%8A%D8%A8-%D8%B5%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%AD- |access-date=2025-08-09 |website=www.odabasham.net}}</ref> His writings are renowned for their creative portrayal of the clash between East and West, and for presenting Sudanese identity in its finest literary form.

Salih became known for his works that depicted the cultural and civilizational collision between the East and the West. He turned his small Sudanese village into a universal symbol representing issues of identity, [[Social alienation|alienation]], and cultural conflict. His novel ''[[Season of Migration to the North]]'' (1966) is considered to be one of the most significant works in [[modern Arabic literature]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Lynx Qualey|first=Marcia|date=2018-11-19|title=On Banipal's '100 Best Arabic Novels'|url=https://arablit.org/2018/11/19/on-banipals-100-best-arabic-novels/|access-date=2021-12-03|website=ArabLit & ArabLit Quarterly|language=en-US}}</ref> The novel gained global recognition and has been translated into multiple languages,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Results for 'au:tayeb salih' [WorldCat.org]|url=https://www.worldcat.org/search?q=au:tayeb+salih&fq=&dblist=638&fc=ln:_25&qt=show_more_ln:&cookie|access-date=2021-12-03|website=www.worldcat.org|language=en}}</ref> and has been studied in universities worldwide.<ref>Waïl S. Hassan, Tayeb Salih: Ideology and the Craft of Fiction, Syracuse University Press, 2003.</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=On Banipal’s ‘100 Best Arabic Novels’|url=https://arablit.org/2018/11/19/on-banipals-100-best-arabic-novels/|access-date=December 3, 2021|publisher=ArabLit & ArabLit Quarterly|date=November 19, 2018|author=Marcia Lynx Qualey|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220104131919/https://arablit.org/2018/11/19/on-banipals-100-best-arabic-novels/|archive-date=January 4, 2022|url-status=live}}</ref>

Tayeb Salih spent his life between the East and the West, living in Britain, Qatar, and France,<ref>[https://www.alarabiya.net/articles/2009/02/18/66699.html Al Arabiya News Channel] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170509225357/http://www.alarabiya.net/articles/2009/02/18/66699.html|date=May 9, 2017}}</ref> and worked for esteemed media and cultural institutions such as the British Broadcasting Corporation ([[BBC]]) and the [[UNESCO]] organization. Throughout his diverse career in literature, media, and education, Salih played a crucial role in bringing the voice of Sudan to the world.

==Biography==
Born in Karmakol, a village on the Nile near [[Al Dabbah, Sudan|Al Dabbah]], Sudan, in the [[Northern state, Sudan|Northern Province of Sudan]],<ref>{{cite news| url=https://www.theguardian.com/books/2009/feb/20/obituary-tayeb-salih | location=London | work=The Guardian | first=Jamal | last=Mahjoub | title=Obituary: Tayeb Salih | date=20 February 2009}}</ref> he graduated from [[University of Khartoum]] with a Bachelor of Science, before leaving for the University of London in the United Kingdom. Coming from a background of small farmers and religious teachers, his original intention was to work in agriculture. However, excluding a brief spell as a schoolmaster before moving to England, he worked in journalism and the promotion of international cultural exchange.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Al-Ṭayyib Ṣāliḥ {{!}} Sudanese writer|url=https://www.britannica.com/biography/al-Tayyib-Salih|access-date=2021-02-26|website=Encyclopedia Britannica|language=en}}</ref>

For more than ten years, Salih wrote a weekly column for the London-based Arabic language newspaper ''[[al Majalla]]'', in which he explored various literary themes. He worked for the [[BBC]]'s Arabic Service and later became director general of the Ministry of Information in Doha, [[Qatar]]. The last ten years of his working career, he spent at [[UNESCO]] headquarters in Paris, where he held various posts and was UNESCO's representative for the [[Arab states of the Persian Gulf]].<ref name=":1" />

==Literary career==

Salih's writing draws important inspiration from his youth in a Sudanese village; life that is centered on rural people and their complex relationships. "At various levels and with varying degrees of psychoanalytic emphasis, he deals with themes of reality and illusion, the [[cultural dissonance]] between the West and the exotic Orient, the harmony and conflict of brotherhood, and the individual's responsibility to find a fusion between his or her contradictions."<ref name="arabworldbooks1">{{cite web|url=http://www.arabworldbooks.com/authors/tayeb_saleh.htm |title=Tayeb Saleh |publisher=Arabworldbooks.com |access-date=2012-10-15}}</ref> Furthermore, the motifs of his books are derived from his religious experience as a [[Muslims|Muslim]] in 20th-century Sudan, both pre- and post-colonial.<ref name="arabworldbooks1"/> Another, more general subject of Salih's writing is the confrontation of the [[Arab world|Arab Muslim]] and the Western European world.<ref>{{cite web|last=Newton|first=Maud|title=Book Review: After the Colonizers depart|url=https://www.npr.org/templates/story/story.php?storyId=104205048|publisher=NPR Books}}</ref>

In 1966, Salih published his novel ''Mawsim al-Hijrah ilâ al-Shimâl ([[Season of Migration to the North]])'', for which he is best known. It was first published in the Beirut journal ''[[Hiwâr]]''. The main concern of the novel is with the impact of [[British colonialism]] and European modernity on rural African societies in general, and on Sudanese culture and identity in particular. His novel reflects the conflicts of modern Sudan and depicts the brutal history of [[European colonialism]] as shaping the reality of contemporary Sudanese society. ''Season of Migration to the North'' is a story told to an unspecified audience by the unnamed narrator, a “traveled man” and an African who has returned after having spent years abroad. He returns to his Sudanese village of Wad Hamid on the [[Nile]] in the 1950s after having written a [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] thesis on ‘the life of an obscure English poet’. Mustafa Sa'eed, the main protagonist of the novel, is a child of British colonialism, and a fruit of colonial education.

In his essay "The New Novel in Sudan", published in [[Banipal]] magazine's issue of spring 1966 on ''Sudanese Literature today'', Sudanese writer Emad Blake remarked that Salih "confronted the crucial issues of his time, such as the clash of Eastern and Western civilizations, as well as boldly employing sex and a style of writing we might term the 'impossible easy'."<ref>{{Cite web|title=Banipal (UK) Magazine of Modern Arab Literature - Back Issues - Banipal 55|url=https://www.banipal.co.uk/back_issues/issue.cfm?publication_id=93|access-date=2021-12-03|website=www.banipal.co.uk}}</ref>

The Damascus-based Arab Literary Academy named it one of the best novels in Arabic of the twentieth century. Upon its publication, it was banned in Salih's native Sudan for several years, because of its partly sexual content and despite the fact that it won him prominence and international fame.<ref name=":0">{{cite web |date=23 February 2009 |title=Tayeb Salih, 80, Cross-Cultural Arabic Novelist, Dies |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2009/02/23/books/23salih.html?mtrref=www.google.se&gwh=860B7C877F4F04A13227627A219945CD&gwt=pay&assetType=REGIWALL |website=The New York Times}}</ref> 

"ʿUrs al-Zayn" (published in English as [[The Wedding of Zein]]) is a novella, published in 1966, centering on the unlikely nuptials of the town eccentric Zein. Tall and odd-looking, with just two teeth in his mouth, Zein has made a reputation for himself as the man who falls in love over and over with girls who promptly marry other men, – to the point where mothers seek him out in hopes that he will draw the eye of available suitors to their eligible daughters.<ref name="review">{{cite web|url=http://www.bostonbibliophile.com/2010/08/review-wedding-of-zein-by-tayeb-salih.html |title=REVIEW: The Wedding of Zein, by Tayeb Salih |publisher=The Boston Bibliophile |date=2010-08-31 |access-date=2012-10-15}}</ref> "The Wedding of Zein" was made into a drama in [[Libya]] and won [[Kuwait]]i filmmaker Khalid Siddiq an award at the [[Cannes Festival|Cannes Film Festival]] in the late 1970s.{{citation needed|date=August 2013}}

In his reflections on Salih's literary style, his translator [[Denys Johnson-Davies]] wrote that Salih "exploited to the full the richness of the literary language in his narrative and uses the vivid local dialect for his dialog. [...] Tayeb Salih’s work shows his wide reading in the byways of Arabic literature, including poetry, which has helped to fashion a style which is direct and fluent, a style which an Arab critic has described as being closer to dramatic writing than that of the novel."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lynx Qualey |first=Marcia |date=2014-07-14 |title=Denys Johnson-Davies on How Tayeb Salih Got His Start |url=https://arablit.org/2014/07/14/denys-johnson-davies-on-how-tayeb-salih-got-his-start/ |access-date=2022-05-24 |website=ArabLit & ArabLit Quarterly |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Awards in honour of Tayeb Salih ==
[[File:جائزة_الطيب_صالح_العالمية_للإبداع_الكتابي.jpg|thumb|Logo of the al-Tayeb Salih Award for Creative Writing]]
In 1998, a group of Salih's friends formed a committee to honour him, and collected $20,000 for his personal use. He chose to use the money to establish the Tayeb Salih Creative Writing Award.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.akmcc.com/jjoomla/index.php/tayeb-salih-book-prize |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130407162929/http://www.akmcc.com/jjoomla/index.php/tayeb-salih-book-prize |url-status=dead |archive-date=2013-04-07 |title=SKRyzzer Was Here |publisher=Akmcc.com |access-date=2013-11-06 }}</ref> 

Awarded since 2002, the ''al-Tayeb Salih Prize for Literary Creativity'' is a literary prize for Sudanese novels, presented by the Abdel Karim Mirghani Cultural Center in [[Omdurman]], and is dedicated to first novels by emerging Sudanese writers.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-09-06|title=Interview with novelist Sara El Jak on literature,...|url=https://bookpublishing.piyasaa.com/interview-with-novelist-sara-el-jak-on-literature/|access-date=2021-12-03|website=Book Publishing|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=جائزة الطيب صالح للإبداع الروائي|url=http://www.akmcc.com/index.php/ar/2021-07-14-04-11-07/2021-07-14-05-42-12|access-date=2021-12-03|website=www.akmcc.com}}</ref>

Since 2010, another award, called the [[Tayeb Salih International Award]], has been granted to outstanding [[Modern Arabic literature|modern Arab writers]] in the fields of novel, short story, and critical studies.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Winners Of Al-Tayeb Salih Creative Writing Award Announced{{!}} Sudanow Magazine|url=http://sudanow-magazine.net/page.php?subId=9&Id=368|access-date=2021-01-13|website=sudanow-magazine.net}}</ref> The award has been sponsored by telecommunications company Zain Sudan<ref>{{Cite web|last=Zain Sudan Telecom|title=El Tayeb Salih Award|url=https://www.sd.zain.com/English/About/Pages/ElTayebSalehAward-Tab.aspx}}</ref> and has been critically seen by some Sudanese intellectuals, calling it “an attempt to control the Sudanese cultural scene” by the Ministry of Culture.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Lynx Qualey|first=Marcia|date=2015-02-24|title=On the Heels of the Sudanese Writers Union Shutdown, Glittering Literary Awards|url=https://arablit.org/2015/02/24/on-the-heels-of-the-sudanese-writers-union-shutdown-glittering-literary-awards/|access-date=2021-01-13|website=ArabLit & ArabLit Quarterly|language=en}}</ref>

== Death ==
Salih died on 18 February 2009 in London. His body was buried on 20 February in Sudan, where the funeral ceremony was attended by a large number of prominent personalities and Arab writers, as well as the then Sudanese President [[Omar al-Bashir|Omar Al-Bashir]], writer and former Prime Minister [[Sadiq al-Mahdi|Sadiq Al Mahdi]], and [[Muhammad Othman Al-Mirghani]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|last=Flood|first=Alison|date=2009-02-19|title=Sudanese novelist Tayeb Salih dies aged 80|url=http://www.theguardian.com/books/2009/feb/19/fiction-sudan|access-date=2021-01-13|website=the Guardian|language=en}}</ref>
